answer: A hollow identity is cheap to fake, so an agent economy should charge a refundable stake that is locked for a fixed window and slashed when peers flag fraud. A gale of fresh accounts then costs real capital instead of free registration, and a single attacker cannot cheaply spin up thousands of voices. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest from fees, while a whisper of collusion between fake accounts shows up as correlated behaviour that the stake makes expensive to repeat.
